idh.reasoning: For IDH status considered independently, the metadata favors IDH-wildtype because the patient is older and the tumor shows an aggressive imaging phenotype: marked enhancement, substantial enhancing tumor volume, necrotic/non-enhancing core, extensive edema, midline crossing, ependymal invasion, deep white-matter invasion, multiple satellites, and large whole-tumor volume. These features are more typical of IDH-wildtype diffuse glioma than lower-grade IDH-mutant glioma. Features arguing against this are the frontal cortical location and cortical involvement, which can be seen in IDH-mutant diffuse gliomas, especially frontal tumors. Overall, the aggressive enhancing, necrotic, edematous, infiltrative pattern outweighs the location-based counterevidence.

Molecular calls remain probabilistic because DWI/ADC, perfusion, MR spectroscopy, SWI/GRE, and histopathology are not available; calcification, cellularity, rCBV, and 2HG could materially affect confidence, especially for 1p/19q status.
